“Can you tell me about a time you went above and beyond your expected duties?”

(Before we answer this question, let’s pretend the qualities/behaviors the company are looking for are problem solving and initiative and use those to craft our S.T.A.R. interview answer. Also, for our purposes, we are going to separate the answer into the four categories outlined above, but you will not want to do this in the interview. It will all blend together as one unified response).

Situation: I was a part of a team working on a presentation meant to help us secure a major new client for our company. The weather was bad, and as a result my supervisor got caught in a snowstorm and was unable to make it back in time. It looked like we were going to have to cancel the meeting and potentially lose the client.

Task: I had been looking for ways to take on more responsibility, so I volunteered to finish up the presentation.

Action: I worked with my supervisor via the phone and between the two of us, we were able to go ahead with the scheduled meeting.

Result: As a result of my initiative, we not only landed the client, but I was also recommended for a promotion.

So the idea in my opinion is to take your experience and convert it to this format... and have a few answers ready based on your experience... and when you get a question, try to use one of your answers that best fits that question
Check out Amazon's leadership principles...
https://www.amazon.jobs/en/principles
amazon.jobs

And write a story that exemplifies each principle

I was contacted by the recruiter ( amazon)yesterday and was verbally offered the position. I wanted to list my experience here and thank you all for this awesome platform:                                   1. Phone screen - a lot of LP style questions, resume review, no system design question but I made sure to give 1-2 examples of projects that were highly technical and focused on my skill sets of Project Management and Requirement and process analysis. Focus on your best projects. My HM was impressed in an hour phone screening and  immediately mentioned at the end of the interview that he is moving me forward for a loop . I have to say, he started being very tight and difficult, but as we navigated more and as he learned more about my experience, he loosened up. So, do not get scared but be confident and give your best answer and refer to the best project for that question/scenario. The frame of mind in remembering all your projects and picking the best for the scenario is very important 2. Loop interviews - very challenging in terms of making sure that I quote different projects to all 5 interviewers. I noticed a lot of questions were also around how I have failed in situations as a PM and what did I learn and applied in the future. I made sure to use STAR format and didn't shy away from referring to my mistakes in my career. The system design questions was very basic. my biggest challenge was making sure I have different projects for every scenario with every single interviewer. All my 5 interviews went well and the HM used 15minutes of his loop time to prepare me for the other 4 people.HM disclosed the lps for other interviewers as well . I didn't ask , he volunteered himself. Happy to help if you have any further question

do mock interviews and get feedback from your interviewing partner; ask them to give you brutally honest feedback if your answer isn't delivering. 
Also, record yourself answering this question and play it back to continuously optimize your answer.

Assuming you have led 0-1 programs, I would start with delivering your methodology in a crisp way in about 1-2 minutes. Key is to clearly state with the interviewer that you are going to stay high level and that you can drill into any specific stage based on where they'd like to spend the time on. 
However you need to land the fundamentals in that first couple of min : the why (goals, business case, etc.), the what (eliciting FRs and NFRs, risks, dependencies, etc.) and the how (comms, governance, decision making, escalation, testing, rollout, monitoring, etc.)

messages.content: Hey folks have PM-T interview coming up with Amazon, anyone knows if PM-Ts have system design as well?

What to Prep For:

Basic Project Management type questions – managing scope, budget and how you mitigate risk!
Be able to speak to your resume and overall experience
Situational/Behavioral Questions – “Tell me about a time you had to meet or work with a difficult stakeholder”   “Tell us about  a time you had to be resourceful on a project”
When answering questions with them I would utilize the STAR method – walk them through you answer outlining what the situation was, what you were tasked with, what you did and what the outcome was!
Be confident in answering and be yourself! Again, personality is big with this group. They are looking for someone who has that drive as a Project Manager and is not afraid to jump in and take charge to deliver on a Project.
They may ask a few questions around how you stay organized when tackling a few projects – different tools you have used, etc
